title: nVNS Trial in UC-IBS Overlap Patients
official: Randomized Trial of Non-Invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation in UC-IBS and Mild Ulcerative Colitis: NIH Aim 3
summary: Many people with ulcerative colitis (UC) continue to experience symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloating, and bowel urgency, even when there is little or no active inflammation in their intestines. Researchers believe that communication between the brain, nervous system, and gut may play an important role in these ongoing symptoms. The purpose of this study is to determine whether 8 weeks of non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation changes brain activity and communication within networks that regulate digestion, pain, and body functions such as heart rate. Researchers will also evaluate whether these changes are associated with improvements in gastrointestinal symptoms, nervous system function, and markers of inflammation. Participation in this study involves random assignment to a study group for 8 weeks and then followed for an additional 4 weeks after completing the intervention. The study aims to assess the effects of the intervention using brain imaging, wearable device measurements, laboratory tests for inflammation, and questionnaires about symptoms and quality of life. The goal is to better understand how the brain-gut connection contributes to persistent symptoms in ulcerative colitis and whether non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation may help improve those symptoms.
conditions: Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Ulcerative Colitis Type
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 through 65 years at consent

Able to understand and provide informed consent in English.

Ability and willingness to provide informed consent and comply with study procedures.

Willing and able to complete questionnaires, biospecimen collection, wearables monitoring, MRI procedures, and other study requirements.

Meets one of the phenotype definitions:

UC-IBS: Previous histologic confirmation of UC; Fecal calprotectin \<150ug/g; Rome V positive for IBS symptoms

Mild UC: Previous histologic confirmation of UC; Fecal calprotectin 150-250 µg/g; partial Mayo Clinic Score 2-4

Willingness to avoid elective changes in medications taken specifically for GI symptoms for at least 2 weeks before baseline, unless a change is medically required.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Inability or unwillingness to provide informed consent or complete study procedures in English.

BMI \>35.

Anticipated need for surgery or another major medical intervention within 1 month of enrollment.

History of surgery within the preceding 6 months.

Presence of a major, active psychiatric diagnosis (e.g., PTSD, schizophrenia, Bipolar, OCD).

Initiation of new psychiatric medication or new dosage within \< 3 months of study participation.

Medical comorbidity judged to materially interfere with HRV or interpretation of autonomic outcomes including: cardiac disease or related (e.g., heart failure, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, clinically significant hypertension, hypotension, bradycardia, or tachycardia)

Current use of medications with a direct and substantial effect on heart rate, cardiac autonomic regulation, or brain function that, in the investigator's judgment, would materially interfere with interpretation of HRV or neuroimaging outcomes. Examples include beta-adrenergic blockers, ivabradine, digoxin, Class I or III antiarrhythmic agents, non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers (e.g., verapamil or diltiazem), centrally acting sympatholytic agents (e.g., clonidine or guanfacine), and regularly used stimulant medications (e.g., amphetamine or methylphenidate). Use of antidepressants commonly prescribed in this population, including SSRIs, SNRIs, and tricyclic antidepressants, will be permitted provided the participant has been on a stable dose for at least 30 days before enrollment and no dose change is anticipated during the study assessment period.

Use of steroid medication within 4 weeks of study initiation or initiation of steroid medication during study period.

Current tobacco use \>1/2 pack of cigarettes per day or alcohol abuse.

Females only: Pregnancy

Any standard institutional contraindication to MRI identified during MRI safety screening including: a non-removable ferromagnetic implant or device, implants without documentation, prior significant tattoo-related heating or burns, movement disorder, severe claustrophobia that cannot be managed, or another condition judged unsafe for MRI.

Changes in medications taken specifically for GI symptoms within 2 weeks before baseline, unless a change is medically required.

Use of antibiotics within 1 month of study participation

Use of probiotics within 1 month of study participation

Current participation in another IBS or UC-specific intervention study or planned initiation of a new IBS or UC-directed treatment during the 8-week randomized period.

Contraindication to cervical nVNS or inability to use the device safely.

Dermatologic conditions affecting the neck region that would interfere with nVNS placement

Any implanted electrical device

Any metallic device implanted at or near the neck

History of cervical vagotomy

Use of another electrical device at the same time (e.g., TENS unit, muscle stimulator) or any portable electronic device

Movement disorder
